title: The Weil Ground State on a Finite Window: Certified Interlacing with the Zeros of ζ
content: Let \( \mathcal Q_a \) be Weil's quadratic form on \( L^2(-a,a) \) and \( F=\hat f \) the Fourier transform of a function at the bottom of its spectrum. Connes, Consani and Moscovici observed that the zeros of \( F \) approximate the zeros of \( \zeta \), and Connes and van Suijlekom proved that they are real when the bottom is simple, isolated and even. We study this ground state at the support \( a \) = 1.82, where positivity of \( \mathcal Q_a \) is certified and the Weil form of the Davenport–Heilbronn function is negative. For the certified extremal vector \( z \) of the lower form, we evaluate \( F_z \) in ball arithmetic on balls containing the first 256 zeros \( \gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_{256} \) of \( \zeta \), i.e. all zeros up to 478.94\( \approx2t_c \), \( t_c=2\pi e^{2a} \). All 256 signs are determined, with a margin of \( 4.9\cdot10^{51} \) against the radii, and they alternate. Hence \( F_z \) has a zero in each of the 255 gaps \( (\gamma_j,\gamma_{j+1}) \). A winding-number count shows numerically that there is exactly one, so all zeros of \( F_z \) below \( 2t_c \) are real, simple and interlace with those of \( \zeta \), shifted to one side. We describe the structure behind this: \( F_z/\Xi \) behaves locally as a Nevanlinna function, with residues \( F_z(\gamma)/\Xi'(\gamma) \) of one sign obeying \( \log|F_z(\gamma)\Xi'(\gamma)|=c-\beta\gamma^2 \), \( \beta e^{2a}\approx0.021 \); the interlacing stops at \( 2t_c \), exactly where the shift of the zeros reaches half a spacing. Only the sign alternation is a theorem; the rest is numerical.
